title: 18. Mean, Median and Mode of Ungrouped Data

q.t: Find the mean of 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12.
q.e: Sum 40 ÷ 5 values. The mean is the equal share.

q.t: Find the median of 3, 7, 9, 12 and 15.
q.e: The middle value of the ordered data.

q.t: Find the mode of 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 3.
q.e: The value that occurs most often.

q.t: Find the mean of the first five natural numbers.
Find the median of 2, 4, 6 and 8.
q.e: With an even count, average the two middle values.

q.t: The mean of 6 numbers is 7. Find their sum.
q.e: Sum = mean × number of values.

q.t: The mean of a set of observations equals:
o: Sum of observations ÷ number of observations
q.e: It shares the total equally.

q.t: Find the median of 5, 1 and 9.
q.e: Arrange first: 1, 5, 9.

q.t: The value that occurs most frequently in a data set is the:
q.e: Mode means the most ‘fashionable’ value.

q.t: Find the range of 12, 7, 19 and 4.
Find the mean of the first ten natural numbers.
Find the mean of the first five prime numbers.
The mean of 6, 8, x, 12 and 14 is 10. Find x.
q.e: The sum must be 50: x = 50 − 40.
14 occurs four times; 18 occurs three times.

q.t: Values 1, 2 and 3 occur with frequencies 2, 3 and 5. Find the mean.
The mean of 5 numbers is 20. If 4 is added to each number, find the new mean.
q.e: The total rises by 5 × 4, so the mean rises by 4.

q.t: The mean of 5 numbers is 20. If each number is multiplied by 3, find the new mean.
q.e: The total is tripled, so the mean is tripled.

q.t: Find the median of the first eight even natural numbers.
q.e: 2, 4, …, 16: the 4th and 5th are 8 and 10.

q.t: For a data set, mean = 20 and median = 22. Using the empirical relation Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, find the mode.
The mean of 20 observations is 15. One observation, 20, is replaced by 40. Find the new mean.
q.e: The total rises by 20, so the mean rises by 20 ÷ 20 = 1.

q.t: The mean of 25 observations was found to be 78.4. Later, one observation 96 was found to have been misread as 69. Find the correct mean.
q.e: The total was 27 too small. 27 ÷ 25 = 1.08, so the mean is 78.4 + 1.08.

q.t: The mean of 11 results is 60. The mean of the first six is 58 and of the last six is 63. Find the sixth result.
q.e: 348 + 378 counts the sixth twice; the true total is 660. 726 − 660.

q.t: The data 24, 25, 26, x + 2, x + 3, 30, 31, 34 is in ascending order and its median is 27.5. Find x.
q.e: Median = average of the 4th and 5th: (2x + 5) ÷ 2 = 27.5.

q.t: The mean of x, x + 3, x + 6, x + 9 and x + 12 is 10. Find x.
q.e: The mean of equally spaced values is the middle one: x + 6 = 10.

q.t: Values 5, 10, 15, 20 have frequencies 2, 5, p, 2 and the mean is 12.5. Find p.
The average of five consecutive even numbers is 30. Find the smallest.
q.e: The middle one is 30: 26, 28, 30, 32, 34.

q.t: The mean of 100 items is 50. Each item is doubled and then 5 is subtracted. Find the new mean.
q.e: The mean follows the same steps: 2 × 50 − 5.

q.t: 30 boys have mean mark 60 and 20 girls have mean mark 70. Find the mean mark of all 50.
The mean of 5 numbers is 27. When one number is left out, the mean of the rest is 25. Find the number left out.
The mean of 9 observations is 12. The first is increased by 1, the second by 2, and so on up to the ninth by 9. Find the new mean.
q.e: The total rises by 1 + 2 + … + 9 = 45, so the mean rises by 5.

q.t: The data 2, 4, x, 12, 14 is in ascending order and its mean equals its median. Find x.
q.e: Median = x. Mean = (32 + x) ÷ 5 = x, so 4x = 32.

q.t: The sum of the deviations of a set of values from 25 is 25, and from 35 is −25. How many values are there?
q.e: Σx − 25n = 25 and Σx − 35n = −25. Subtracting: 10n = 50.

q.t: The sum of the deviations of a set of values from 25 is 25, and from 35 is −25. Find their mean.
q.e: n = 5 and Σx = 25 + 125 = 150, so the mean is 30.

q.t: For a data set, mode = 50 and mean = 41. Using Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, find the median.
The mean of 13 observations is 14. The mean of the first seven is 12 and of the last seven is 16. Find the seventh.
The mean of the first n natural numbers is 20. Find n.
q.e: The mean of 1 to n is (n + 1) ÷ 2 = 20.

q.t: The sum of the deviations of all observations from their own mean is always:
q.e: Σ(x − mean) = Σx − n × mean = Σx − Σx.

q.t: The mean of x and 1/x is M. The mean of x² and 1/x² is:
q.e: x + 1/x = 2M. Squaring: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 4M², so (x² + 1/x²) ÷ 2 = 2M² − 1.

q.t: A data set of 11 different values has median 40. The four largest values are each increased by 10. Find the new median.
q.e: The median is the 6th value. Only the 8th to 11th change, so the middle one is untouched.
